Package edu.iu.validation

package edu.iu.validation
Deep bean validation over the Jakarta Validation constraint vocabulary.

IuValidator walks a business object graph by bean property, evaluates every constraint annotation it finds, and collects all failures into one IuValidationResult. Nothing short-circuits: a single pass reports every property that failed and which rule each value failed on. 

final var result = IuValidator.validate(EnrlHeader.class, header);
if (!result.isValid())
        LOG.warning(result.report());

The constraint annotations are read as a vocabulary only. This is not a Validator implementation: there is no ValidatorFactory, no validation.xml, and no provider discovery.

What is validated

Bean properties are discovered exactly as edu.iu.client.IuJsonAdapter discovers them for JSON binding — the full interface and superclass hierarchy, nearest declaration winning on name collision — so the set of validated properties always matches the set of serialized properties. Constraints are honored on the read method, the write method, and the backing field.

Valid cascades into a property value. Cascading descends Iterable, arrays, Map keys and values, and Optional. Object graph cycles terminate on instance identity rather than overflowing the stack.

Standalone annotation targets

IuValidator.validate(java.lang.reflect.AnnotatedElement, Object) validates a value the caller already holds against the constraints on the target that declares it — a field, the return value of a getter, a method argument — with no bean to walk from. Only that target's own annotations apply; nothing is unioned from the enclosing type. 

IuValidator.require(parameter, "message", argument);

A Class target is validated as a bean instead, so the generic entry point is a superset of the type-based one rather than a parallel path. Container element constraints and Valid cascade behave exactly as they do during a bean walk.

Groups

Only the default group is evaluated. A constraint that declares no groups() belongs to Default and is evaluated; a constraint that names an explicit group is not applicable to the default group and is skipped. payload() is exposed through IuConstraintViolation.attributes() and otherwise ignored.
